chosen_property.label: occurredIn
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the location where an event or action occurred.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property covers the broad range of subjects and objects (locations and times) for this relation; minting a general property.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.comment: A diagnostic test or procedure offered by a diagnostic lab. Also called: lab test, diagnostic offering, test procedure. Examples: "DiagnosticLab 'LabCorp' availableTest 'Blood Test'", "DiagnosticLab 'Imaging Center' availableTest 'MRI Scan'."

candidates.label: typicalTest
candidates.comment: A typical test relation between a medical condition and a medical test commonly performed for that condition. Also called common test, diagnostic test, standard test. candidates.label: gettingTestedInfo
candidates.comment: A getting tested info relation between a special announcement and information regarding testing for a medical condition. Also called: testing information, diagnostic details, screening guidance. candidates.label: identifyingTest
candidates.comment: An identifying test relation between a medical sign and a medical test that can detect it. Also called diagnostic test, detection test, test for sign. candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: subTest
candidates.comment: A component relation between a medical test panel and an individual medical test that is part of the panel. Also called "panel component", "included test", "part of test panel". Examples: "The blood panel has subTest a cholesterol test", "The medical test panel's subTest is a glucose measurement", "This panel includes several subTest procedures."

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: participant

candidates.label: sportsTeam

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer

candidates.label: member

candidates.label: competitor

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: partOfSystem

candidates.label: partOfEpisode

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. candidates.label: partOfSeries

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subStructure

Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: naturalProgression
candidates.comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: scheduledPaymentDate

candidates.label: scheduleTimezone

candidates.label: exceptDate

candidates.label: opens

candidates.label: byDay

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime

candidates.label: departureTime

candidates.label: eventSchedule

candidates.label: timeOfDay

candidates.label: followup

candidates.label: follows

candidates.label: afterMedia

candidates.label: followee

candidates.label: availableThrough

candidates.label: episodeNumber

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: includedRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A risk factor inclusion relation between a medical risk estimator and a risk factor used in its calculation. Also called risk factor in calculation, factor considered, included element. Examples: "A medical risk estimator includes a risk factor of age.", "The estimator considers an included risk factor of smoking.", "This tool uses an included risk factor for calculation."

relations.definition: To be under the authority or command of.
relations.embedding_query_text: controlled by: To be under the authority or command of.

chosen_property.label: legislationResponsible
chosen_property.justification: legislationResponsible runs from legislation to the responsible authority; using it inversely fits a government organization controlled by a political party.

candidates.label: nerveMotor
candidates.comment: A muscle controlled by a nerve through a neurological pathway. Also called motor innervation, controls muscle, innervates muscle. Examples: "Radial Nerve nerveMotor 'Triceps Brachii'", "Musculocutaneous Nerve nerveMotor 'Biceps Brachii'", "Phrenic Nerve nerveMotor 'Diaphragm'". Distinct from nerve, which describes the nerve of a muscle.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: accessibilityControl
candidates.comment: An accessibility control relation between a creative work and the input methods sufficient for its full control. Also called control methods, input compatibility, interaction modes. Examples: "A video game's accessibility control is 'keyboard'.", "A web application's accessibility control is 'mouse'."

candidates.label: legalStatus
candidates.comment: A regulatory status relation between a dietary supplement, drug, or medical entity and its legal classification, including controlled substance schedules. Also called regulatory status, legal classification, controlled substance status, drug schedule. Examples: A drug has a legalStatus of 'PrescriptionOnly'. A dietary supplement has a legalStatus of 'OverTheCounter'. A medication has a legalStatus of 'Schedule II controlled substance'. Distinct from drugClass, which is a medical classification, not a legal one.

candidates.label: jurisdiction
candidates.comment: A legal scope relation between a government service or legislation and the administrative area or territory where it applies. Also called legal authority, governing area, applicable region, domain of law. Examples: A government service has a jurisdiction of 'California'. Legislation has a jurisdiction of 'United States federal law'. A permit applies to the jurisdiction of 'City of London'. Distinct from eligibleRegion or ineligibleRegion, which are about availability, not legal authority.

candidates.label: license
candidates.comment: A licensing relation between a creative work and the license document that applies to its content. Also called: governed by license, licensed under, copyright license. Examples: "Software Project license MIT License", "Image license Creative Commons Attribution 4.0", "Music Track license Public Domain".

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: referee
candidates.comment: A referee relation between a sports event and the person officiating it to enforce rules. Also called officiated by, umpire, judge. Examples: "A football match has a referee 'Pierluigi Collina'.", "A tennis match has a referee 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.", "A basketball game has a referee 'Joey Crawford'."

relations.definition: To require winning or changing.
relations.embedding_query_text: need to flip: To require winning or changing.

chosen_property.label: needToFlip
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that a political party needs to win or change control of a government body.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses the need to flip a political seat or body; minting a new property.

candidates.label: requiredCollateral
candidates.comment: A required collateral relation between a loan or credit and the assets needed to secure its repayment. Also called loan security, collateral for loan. Examples: "A car loan requires collateral 'the vehicle itself'.", "A business loan requires collateral 'company assets'.", "A mortgage requires collateral 'the property'."

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: requiredGender
candidates.comment: A required gender relation between a people audience and the specific gender criteria for inclusion. Also called target gender, gender requirement. Examples: "An event targets a people audience with required gender 'female'.", "A survey specifies a required gender 'male'.", "A product is marketed to a people audience with required gender 'unspecified'."

candidates.label: requiredMaxAge
candidates.comment: A required maximum age relation between a people audience and the upper age limit for inclusion. Also called max age, age limit. Examples: "A children's event targets a people audience with required max age '12'.", "A youth program has a required max age '25'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required max age '99'."

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: physicalRequirement
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the physical activities or abilities required for a job posting. Also called physical demands, fitness requirements, job physicality. Examples: A job posting has a physical requirement of 'ability to lift 50 lbs'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'standing for long periods'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'manual dexterity'.

candidates.label: returnPolicySeasonalOverride
candidates.comment: A temporary modification or override of a standard merchant return policy for a specific season or period. Also called seasonal return policy change, temporary return policy, holiday return policy. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Holiday Return Policy 2023`, `Summer Sale Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Extended Return Window`, `Black Friday Policy` returnPolicySeasonalOverride `Special Return Terms`.

candidates.label: renegotiableLoan
candidates.comment: A renegotiable loan relation indicating whether the interest payment terms of a loan or credit can be changed during its duration. Also called flexible terms, adjustable loan. Examples: "A business loan is a renegotiable loan 'true'.", "A fixed-rate mortgage is a renegotiable loan 'false'.", "A personal line of credit is a renegotiable loan 'true'."

candidates.label: requiredMinAge
candidates.comment: A required minimum age relation between a people audience and the lower age limit for inclusion. Also called min age, age requirement. Examples: "An adult event targets a people audience with required min age '18'.", "A driving course has a required min age '16'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required min age '65'."
